ERPNext · Assets · Asset Workspace

Asset Module User Guide

How to record the laptops, monitors, phones and software subscriptions the company gives its people, hand them out, take them back and see what they cost, step by step from an empty catalogue to an assigned laptop.

MACBOOK AIR M1 - 005
1Category› 2Sub-category› 3Item› 4Asset› 5Submit› 6Assign› 7Return

Before you start

Every asset belongs to four levels. This guide builds one laptop through all of them, using the company’s real records as the example:

1 · CategoryIT HardwareAsset Category
2 · Sub-CategoryLaptopItem Group
3 · ItemMacbook Air M1Item
4 · AssetMACBOOK AIR M1 - 005Asset

The blue line under each level is the ERPNext form you fill in for it.

  • Category: the big group, such as IT Hardware or Subscriptions.
  • Sub-Category: a kind of thing inside it, such as Laptop, Monitor or Design Software.
  • Item: the model or product, such as Macbook Air M1 or Figma Professional.
  • Asset: one physical laptop, or one subscription seat. It is named after its item with a running number: the fifth Macbook Air M1 is Macbook Air M1 - 005.
Most of the time you only do steps 4 to 7

Categories, sub-categories and items are set up once. After that, buying another Macbook means only creating the asset (step 4) and assigning it (step 6).

Who can do what

What you can do depends on your ERPNext role. If a button is missing or you see “You do not have permission”, ask your system manager for the role in this table.

To do thisYou need one of these roles
Open the Asset Workspace and see reportsAccounts User, Accounts Manager, Quality Manager, Stock Manager, System Manager
Create a categoryAccounts User, Accounts Manager, Quality Manager
Create a sub-category or an itemItem Manager
Create and submit assetsAccounts User, Quality Manager
Assign and return assetsAccounts Manager, Stock Manager, System Manager

The Asset Workspace screen

Open it in any of these ways:

  • Click Asset Workspace in the left sidebar of the Assets module.
  • Press Ctrl + G, type Asset Workspace and press Enter.

It opens inside ERPNext like any other page. Every screen has the same parts:

  • Page title and buttons at the top. The main action is the dark button on the right, for example Assign & Return or New Asset.
  • The ⋯ menu next to it: Asset List, Asset Movement List, Employee List and this User Guide.
  • Tabs: Dashboard, Assign & Return, Employees, Assets, Reports, Catalogue.
  • Filters under the tabs on screens that have them: a search box and drop-downs.

Steps 1 to 4 start from the Catalogue tab, which shows every category with its sub-categories and items and has a button for each step.

Set up once

Step 1Create a category

A category is the top group, for example IT Hardware or Subscriptions. Create one only when the company starts tracking a new kind of asset.

  1. Open the Catalogue tab and click New Asset Category at the top right.
  2. Fill in the form as described below.
  3. Click Save (or press Ctrl + S), then go back to the Asset Workspace. The category now appears in the Catalogue.
FieldWhat to enter
Asset Category Name *The name of the group, for example IT Hardware. Its sub-categories are filed under a group with this same name, so choose it carefully; it is hard to change later.
Category TypeHardware for physical things (laptops, monitors, phones). Subscription for software seats and licences. Subscriptions get a renewal date and a monthly or yearly billing cycle, and the reports treat their cost as a running cost.
Enable Capital Work in Progress Accounting leave offAn accounting option for assets that are built over time. Not used for IT equipment.
Non Depreciable CategoryTick it for a Subscriptions category, because software seats never lose value over years. Leave it unticked for hardware.
Finance Books leave emptyOnly needed if your accounts team runs depreciation in more than one set of books.
Accounts *Click Add row and fill in one row:
  • Company *: your company, Infinite Locus.
  • Fixed Asset Account *: the account the asset’s value sits in, for example Electronic Equipment - IL.
  • Accumulated Depreciation Account and Depreciation Expense Account: needed only if these assets are depreciated, for example Accumulated Depreciations - IL and Depreciation - IL.
  • Capital Work In Progress Account: leave empty.
If you are not sure which accounts to use, ask your accounts team.

Step 2Create a sub-category

A sub-category is a kind of thing inside a category, for example Laptop, Monitor or Mobile Phone under IT Hardware.

  1. In the Catalogue, find the category and click + Sub-Category on its card.
  2. An Item Group form opens with the category already filled in as its parent. Type the sub-category name.
  3. Click Save, then go back to the Asset Workspace. The sub-category appears under its category.
FieldWhat to enter
Item Group Name *The sub-category name, for example Laptop.
Parent Item Group filled for youThe category, for example IT Hardware. Do not change it: this is what places the sub-category under its category.
Is Group leave offLeave unticked. A sub-category holds items, not further groups.
Item Group Defaults, Taxes leave emptyNot needed for assets.

Step 3Create an item

An item is the model or product, for example Macbook Air M1. You create it once; every Macbook Air M1 the company owns is then an asset of this item.

  1. In the Catalogue, find the sub-category and click + Item on its row.
  2. The Item form opens with the sub-category, the category, Is Fixed Asset ticked and Maintain Stock unticked. Fill in the rest as below.
  3. Click Save, then go back to the Asset Workspace. The item appears under its sub-category with 0 assets.
FieldWhat to enter
Item Code *A unique code for the model. Using the model name keeps it simple, for example Macbook Air M1.
Item NameThe model name as people say it, for example Macbook Air M1. Every asset of this item is named after it: Macbook Air M1 - 001, - 002 and so on.
Myntra / Ajio / Blinkit / Zepto SKU Code leave emptyUsed only for products sold on marketplaces, not for assets.
Item Group * filled for youThe sub-category, for example Laptop.
Default Unit of Measure *Nos (number of pieces).
Maintain Stock offMust stay unticked. Assets are tracked one by one, not as warehouse stock.
Is Fixed Asset onMust stay ticked. Only fixed asset items can have assets.
Auto create assets on purchase leave offLeave unticked; you create each asset yourself in step 4.
Asset Category * filled for youThe category, for example IT Hardware.
Allow Sales, Allow Purchase, Has Variants, Standard Selling Rate leave as isKeep the defaults. Allow Purchase lets the purchasing team buy this item through ERPNext if needed.
Brand (under Description)Optional, for example Apple. It is shown in the Catalogue and reports.
Other tabs (UOM, Tax, Purchasing, Sales, Quality) leave as isNot needed for assets.

Each new asset

Step 4Create the asset

One asset is one physical laptop, monitor or phone, or one subscription seat. If you buy three monitors, create three assets.

  1. In the Catalogue, find the item and click + Asset on its row. You can also click New Asset on the Dashboard or the Assets tab and pick the item yourself.
  2. The Asset form opens with the item filled in, and its category and sub-category appear on their own. Fill in the rest as below.
FieldWhat to enter
Series leave as isKeep .{item_name}. - .###. It names the asset after its item with the next number, for example Macbook Air M1 - 005. The other choice, ACC-ASS-.YYYY.-, gives the old style ACC-ASS-2026-00001.
Item Code * filled for youThe item, for example Macbook Air M1.
Asset Name * filled for youFilled from the item; the running number is added when you save.
Location *Where the asset is kept when nobody has it, for example Head Office. Returned assets go back here.
Company * filled for youYour company, Infinite Locus.
Asset Category, Sub-Category filled for youTaken from the item. You cannot change them here.
Serial No / Licence IDFor hardware, the serial number printed on the device, for example C02H48213. For a subscription, the licence key or account ID. Searchable everywhere in the Asset Workspace.
Asset TypeExisting Asset for something the company already owns that was not bought through an ERPNext Purchase Receipt or Purchase Invoice. If it was bought through ERPNext, leave this empty and pick that Purchase Receipt or Invoice in the Purchase Details instead.
Maintenance Required leave offTick only if this asset needs scheduled maintenance in ERPNext.
Calculate Depreciation leave offTick only if your accounts team wants ERPNext to depreciate this asset; it then asks for depreciation details on the Depreciation tab.
Purchase Date *When the asset was bought (or, for a subscription, when the seat started).
Available for Use Date *The first day it can be given to someone. Usually the same as the purchase date.
Net Purchase Amount *What it cost, for example ₹92,900. For a subscription, the price for one billing cycle, for example ₹770 for one month of Microsoft 365.
Asset Quantity keep 1Always 1: one asset per device or seat.
Warranty / Renewal DateHardware: when the warranty ends. Subscription: the next renewal date. It can be changed later, even after submitting, and drives the “Warranties & Renewals” list on the Dashboard.
Billing Cycle (subscriptions)Subscriptions only: Monthly or Yearly. Leave empty for hardware.
More Info tab: Custodian, Department leave emptyDo not fill these in. The Asset Workspace sets the Custodian (the employee holding the asset) when you assign it in step 6.
More Info tab: Insurance optionalPolicy number, insurer and dates, if the asset is insured.

Step 5Save and submit

  1. Click Save. The asset gets its name, for example MACBOOK AIR M1 - 005, and shows as Draft.
  2. Click Submit and confirm with Yes. The asset is now Submitted and appears as Available in the Asset Workspace.
An asset must be submitted before anyone can have it

Draft assets do not appear in the Available list. The Dashboard counts them under Draft (not submitted); click that card to find and submit them.

Hand out and take back

Step 6Assign to an employee

Assigning records that an employee now holds the asset. ERPNext stores it as an Asset Movement (Issue), and the asset’s Custodian becomes that employee.

  1. Open the Assign & Return tab. Available on the left lists every asset ready to hand out; use the search box or the Category and Sub-Category filters to find it.
  2. Click Assign on the asset’s row. To hand out several at once, tick them and click Assign Selected at the top of the list.
  3. In the window that opens, fill in the fields below and click Assign.
FieldWhat to enter
Asset shownThe asset(s) you picked. If you opened the window from an employee instead, you choose the asset here; only available assets are offered.
Employee *Start typing the person’s name or employee ID and pick them from the list. Only active employees are offered.
Assigned On *The day they received it. Today is filled in; change it if you are recording an earlier hand-over.

A green message at the bottom right confirms it and names the Asset Movement, for example ACC-ASM-2026-00084. The asset moves to With Employees and shows as Assigned.

You can also assign from: an employee’s page (Assign Asset), the Employees list (Assign on a row), or an asset’s page (Assign).

Step 7Return an asset

Returning records that the asset is back with the company. ERPNext stores it as an Asset Movement (Receipt) to the asset’s location, and the Custodian is cleared.

  1. In Assign & Return, find the asset under With Employees and click Return. For several, tick them and click Return Selected.
  2. Check the Returned On date and click Return.
FieldWhat to enter
Asset from … shownThe asset(s) coming back and who had them.
Returned On *The day it was handed back. It cannot be earlier than the day it was assigned.

When someone hands back everything, open their page under Employees and click Return All. An asset’s own page also has a Return button at the top.

Step 8Move to another employee

Return the asset first (step 7), then assign it to the new person (step 6). An asset that someone holds cannot be assigned to another person directly; the Asset Workspace asks you to return it first. The asset’s history keeps both people.

Day to day

Subscriptions

Software seats follow the same eight steps, with a few differences:

  • Category (step 1): set Category Type to Subscription and tick Non Depreciable Category. The company’s category is Subscriptions, with sub-categories such as Productivity Suite, Design Software, Developer Tools and Communication.
  • One asset per seat. Eight Slack seats are eight assets, so each seat can be given to one person.
  • Net Purchase Amount is the price for one billing cycle; set Billing Cycle to Monthly or Yearly. A yearly ₹13,200 Zoom seat counts as ₹1,100 a month in the reports.
  • Warranty / Renewal Date is the next renewal. When the subscription renews, open the asset and move the date on; this works on a submitted asset.
  • Serial No / Licence ID holds the licence key or the account it is registered to, for example ZM-LIC-0002.
  • Free seats still cost money. The Subscription seats report shows what unused seats cost.

Finding assets and people

Dashboard

Number cards for Total Assets, Assigned, Available, Draft (not submitted), Subscriptions / Month and Hardware Value; one card per category showing how much of each sub-category is assigned; a chart of assigned against available; Warranties & Renewals overdue or due within 45 days; and Recent Activity. Click a category card, or Total Assets, to open those assets.

Employees

Every active employee, their department, and how many hardware assets and subscriptions they hold. Filter by name, department, or Holding (holding assets / no assets). Click a person to see what they hold now and everything they held before, with Assign Asset, Return and Return All buttons.

Assets

The asset register: every asset with its item, type, status, holder, warranty or renewal date and cost. Search by asset, item, serial number or employee, or filter by category, sub-category and status. The status cards at the top also filter: click Draft to see only drafts. Click an asset to see its details, who has it and its full history.

Reports

Open the Reports tab and pick a report in the Report drop-down, the first filter under the tabs. Each report shows number cards, a bar chart and a Details table. In the table you can type in the box under any column heading to filter it, use the menu on a heading to sort, and click a name to open that employee or asset. Export Excel at the top downloads exactly the rows the table shows.

ReportAnswersFilters
Cost per employeeWhat each employee costs in hardware and subscriptions, per month and per year, and their subscription spend so far.Category, department, employees holding assets / all
Cost per departmentWhich department costs most, and the cost per employee.Category
Employee asset registerExactly which assets each person holds right now.Category, department
Assignment historyWho held what, from when to when, for how many days.Category, department, date range
Leavers holding assetsWhat to recover from people who have left.Category
Category & sub-categoryWhat each sub-category holds and costs, how much is in use, what is idle.Category
Item utilisationFor each item, how many are in use and what the idle ones are worth.Category
Subscription seatsSeats paid for, seats used, and what the free ones cost.None
Idle assetsAssets nobody is using, and for how long.Category
Renewals & warrantiesWhat renews at what cost, month by month; warranties ending or expired.Category, next 1 to 24 months
Asset ageingHow old the equipment is, and how much is out of warranty.Category

How costs are worked out

Hardware valuethe asset’s Net Purchase Amount
Subscription per monthMonthly: the amount · Yearly: amount ÷ 12
Monthly costsubscriptions per month + hardware value ÷ 36
Annual costmonthly cost × 12
Subscription spend to dateper-month cost × days held ÷ 30.44, for every period the person held the seat
Utilisationassigned units ÷ all units

The 36 months spread a laptop’s price over three years of use, so it can be compared with monthly subscription costs.

Leavers, repairs, disposal

When an employee leaves

  1. Open Reports and choose Leavers holding assets. It lists everything still held by people whose status is no longer Active.
  2. Collect the items, open the person’s page under Employees and click Return All.
  3. Return or cancel their subscription seats so the company stops paying for them.

Repairs

Record repairs with ERPNext’s Asset Repair or Asset Maintenance. While an asset is under repair it shows as Under Repair and cannot be assigned.

Selling or scrapping

Return the asset from the employee first. Then, on the Asset form, use Actions › Sell Asset or Scrap Asset. It then shows as Disposed and drops out of the cost reports.

Asset statuses

StatusMeansWhat you can do
AvailableSubmitted and nobody has it.Assign it.
AssignedAn employee has it.Return it.
DraftSaved but not submitted.Open it and submit it.
Under RepairIn maintenance or out of order.Wait for the repair to finish.
DisposedSold or scrapped.Nothing; it is kept for history.

Questions and errors

An asset I just created is not in the Available list

It is probably still a Draft: open it and click Submit. Assign & Return shows a yellow message with a Show drafts link when drafts exist. Assets that are Under Repair or Disposed are not listed either.

“… is already with [name]. Return it first.”

Someone holds that asset. Return it from them, then assign it to the new person.

“Transaction date can't be earlier than previous movement date”

The date is before the asset’s last assignment or return. Pick a date on or after it; the asset’s page lists those dates under Assignment History.

“… is not submitted yet. Submit the Asset first.”

Only submitted assets can be assigned. Open the asset and submit it.

My new sub-category does not appear under its category

Its Parent Item Group must be the category’s name. Create sub-categories with + Sub-Category in the Catalogue so this is filled in for you.

My new item does not appear in the Catalogue

Check that Is Fixed Asset is ticked and its Item Group is the sub-category. Items created with + Item in the Catalogue have both set.

“You do not have permission for this.”

Your role does not allow that action. See Who can do what and ask your system manager.

Can I undo an assignment made by mistake?

Return the asset with today’s date. Your accounts manager can also cancel the Asset Movement in ERPNext, which puts things back as they were.

I want an asset named the old way (ACC-ASS-2026-00001)

On the Asset form, change Series to ACC-ASS-.YYYY.- before saving.

Glossary

Asset
One physical item or one subscription seat, for example Macbook Air M1 - 001.
Category
The top group (IT Hardware, Subscriptions). Stored as an ERPNext Asset Category.
Sub-Category
A kind of thing in a category (Laptop, Monitor). Stored as an ERPNext Item Group.
Item
The model or product (Macbook Air M1), marked as a Fixed Asset item.
Custodian
The employee who holds an asset right now.
Asset Movement
ERPNext’s record of an asset changing hands. Issue gives it to an employee; Receipt brings it back.
Existing Asset
An asset the company owned before it was entered in ERPNext, with no purchase document.
Save / Submit
Save keeps a draft you can still change. Submit confirms it; a submitted record can only be cancelled, not edited.
Billing Cycle
How often a subscription is paid: Monthly or Yearly.
Utilisation
The share of units that are assigned to someone.
